description: C1's EDGE/ERROR clause requires: 'Gemini socket error/close mid-call → log; if it drops before any audio, attempt ONE reconnect, else end the call cleanly.' The implementation registers BOTH a 'error' and a 'close' handler on the same Gemini WebSocket instance, and BOTH call the identical onGeminiEnd(reason) function (server.js:426-427). Node's `ws` client emits 'error' THEN 'close' for the SAME underlying connection failure (a single dropped/failed socket fires both events, not two independent failures) — this is standard WebSocket-client semantics (WHATWG WebSocket spec: an error event is followed by a close event for the same failure; well-documented `ws` package behavior). Trace of the actual runtime sequence for the FIRST (and only) real failure: (1) 'error' fires → onGeminiEnd('err ...') → gotAudio=false, geminiReconnects(0)<1, carrierWs OPEN → branch taken: geminiReconnects becomes 1, gemini=null, openGeminiLive() is called, which constructs a brand-new WebSocket and returns immediately (the TCP/TLS handshake is async, so no audio/open has happened yet). (2) Immediately after, 'close' fires on the SAME now-defunct OLD socket object (its own close handler, captured in the earlier openGeminiLive() closure) → onGeminiEnd('closed') runs AGAIN → now geminiReconnects is already 1, so `geminiReconnects < 1` is FALSE → the code falls into the else branch and calls `carrierWs.close()` — ending the call immediately, before the freshly-opened reconnect socket has had any chance to complete its handshake, send setup, or receive audio. Net effect: the 'attempt ONE reconnect' safety net described by C1 is a no-op in practice — a single real Gemini-drop terminates the call on the very first failure (via the paired close event), while silently burning a second Gemini Live session that never gets used and is left orphaned (its own later open/error/close events will find carrierWs already closed). This directly contradicts the C1 EDGE/ERROR invariant and undermines Goal 1's reliability claim.
